chapters.screen: Perceptron. The perceptron reads passengers one at a time. When it gets one wrong it nudges its weights towards the right answer; when it is right it does nothing. Watch the boundary jump around as mistakes come in.
chapters.spoken: Perceptron. The perceptron reads passengers one at a time. When it gets one wrong it nudges its weights towards the right answer; when it is right it does nothing. Watch the boundary jump around as mistakes come in.

chapters.screen: Each mark is one passenger: age (x) and fare paid (y, log scale); women on the left, men on the right. Blue dots survived, red crosses did not.
chapters.spoken: Each mark is one passenger: age and fare paid on a log scale; women on the left, men on the right. Blue dots survived, red crosses did not.

chapters.screen: After the first 60 passengers: a rough first boundary. The shading is a score, not a probability: blue means the 'survived' side, red the other.
chapters.spoken: After the first 60 passengers: a rough first boundary. The shading is a score, not a probability: blue means the 'survived' side, red the other.

chapters.screen: Each frame is real online training: the first epoch every 60 passengers, then one frame per epoch. The data cannot be split perfectly, so the boundary never settles.
chapters.spoken: Each frame is real online training: the first epoch every 60 passengers, then one frame per epoch. The data cannot be split perfectly, so the boundary never settles.

chapters.screen: Validation picked epoch 0.96: train accuracy 76%, validation 75%. A perceptron keeps moving, so the best epoch is kept.
chapters.spoken: Validation picked epoch 0.96: train accuracy 76%, validation 75%. A perceptron keeps moving, so the best epoch is kept.

chapters.screen: An unseen passenger: add bias + weight × input with the kept epoch's weights. A positive score means 'survived'; its size is not a probability.
chapters.spoken: An unseen passenger: add bias plus weight times input with the kept epoch's weights. A positive score means 'survived'; its size is not a probability.

chapters.screen: Final exam: the trained model judges all 210 test passengers it has never seen. Wrong calls are circled on the maps and crossed in the grid, grouped by class of travel.
chapters.spoken: Final exam: the trained model judges all 210 test passengers it has never seen. Wrong calls are circled on the maps and crossed in the grid, grouped by class of travel.

chapters.screen: The perceptron's score is a flat, tilted plane for each sex: two parallel planes, offset by the effect of sex. Height is the model's score, one sheet per sex, seen by a swinging camera.
chapters.spoken: The perceptron's score is a flat, tilted plane for each sex: two parallel planes, offset by the effect of sex. Height is the model's score, one sheet per sex, seen by a swinging camera.

chapters.screen: About the same: 80% with every input against 79% with age, fare and sex.
chapters.spoken: About the same: 80% with every input against 79% with age, fare and sex.

chapters.screen: The perceptron learns from its mistakes alone; on data that cannot be separated it never stops moving. Limitation: it gives no probabilities and no margin, and on overlapping classes its weights keep oscillating, so the result depends on when you stop.
chapters.spoken: The perceptron learns from its mistakes alone; on data that cannot be separated it never stops moving. Limitation: it gives no probabilities and no margin, and on overlapping classes its weights keep oscillating, so the result depends on when you stop.
